note: Trigger delivery receipts (trigger-runner). self_managed: the storage janitor never rotates the live file — rotating it would drop the 7-day dedupe window and in-flight claims and re-deliver triggers; it only expires already-rotated segments by ttl_days. The catalog used to call this self-bounding, but daemon-recovery idempotency keys used to embed daemon+status+minute — every tick minted a NEW key, so latest-per-key compaction never shrank the file (4.9MB). daemon_watchdog now keys recovery per unhealthy episode (stale: last heartbeat timestamp plus a 15-minute retry bucket, at most 4 attempts; missing/malformed: 15-minute bucket — daemonRecoveryKey). trigger-runner rotates inline, under its store lock, once the journal passes its retention threshold (TRIGGER_STORE_DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES, 4MB) and the rotation frees at least max(threshold/4, half the journal): only the dropped records move to a <stem>-YYYYMMDD-HHmmss.jsonl segment (segment + live = the old journal) and the live file keeps every finished receipt younger than 7 days (stable keys never re-deliver inside the window) and every pending claim whose lease expired less than 7 days ago; above target the oldest cron (minute-scoped) receipts are trimmed first. MSN-STORE-BOUNDS: there is no append cap and no fixed read window — dedupe scans backward to 7 days plus the 24h max claim lease, so the journal size never fails a read or an append; growth past TRIGGER_STORE_GROWTH_WARN_BYTES is ops-health trigger-store-growth (warn), with pnpm kyberion scheduler trigger-store rotate (approval-gated) as the manual rotation. Segments expire at 30d (runtime top-level files have no dir sweep, so ttl_days here governs the segments).
